purpose: A record on a mat: the Radiant Vinyl Grooves shader paints a spinning LP whose grooves catch the light, two ink hands tell the time over it and a tonearm plays one side per hour, landing on the lead-in at :00 and reaching the run-out before the hour turns. It refuses digits, ticks and a second hand: the spinning grooves are the motion.

accent.where: the groove sheen the shader paints, prismatic or warm by the shimmer option

night.recipe: The mat flips with --face-bg and the tells read --face-ink-muted. The record is content and stays dark in both palettes, so the hands and the arm read --sheet-ink, the role that does not invert, never --face-ink.

options.intent: 33 is the LP default; 45 only when the faster groove shimmer is wanted, the hands and arm do not change.
prismatic shows the diffraction rainbow the grooves really make; warm desaturates it to one sheen for a calmer dial or a bedroom.

antiPatterns.rule: Never read --face-ink for anything drawn over the record
antiPatterns.why: the record is dark in both palettes, so the day palette's black ink vanishes on it; --sheet-ink is the mode-stable role for a surface that does not flip

antiPatterns.rule: Do not add a second hand or a seconds readout
antiPatterns.why: the record already spins at real 33 rpm; a second motion on the dial competes with it and the face stops being a turntable

antiPatterns.rule: Do not let the shader draw the tonearm, numerals or any ink
antiPatterns.why: the page cannot read the kiosk tokens, so anything it draws is hardcoded colour; everything that must respond to the palette is drawn by React over the frame

antiPatterns.rule: Do not keep the frame alive while the face is inactive
antiPatterns.why: a WebGL page redraws every frame; the clock app swaps faces and apps for weeks on a Pi, so the frame pauses when inactive and unmounts a minute later
